tier_reason: First-party README tables (roundtrip vs @mysten/bcs, 300K iterations on Bun; raw serializeInto vs @mysten serialize) with no benchmark code in the repo (src/ and test/ hold only bcs.test.ts and compat.test.ts), no @mysten/bcs version, Bun version or CPU stated; the linked live benchmark bcs-benchmark.vercel.app does not resolve (ENOTFOUND).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Roundtrip (serialize plus deserialize) vs @mysten/bcs, 300K iterations on Bun: SimpleStruct (41 B) 10.7M vs 1.3M ops/s (7.9x), NestedStruct 4.3M vs 608K (7.1x), Enum 9.6M vs 1.3M (7.3x), u64 7.0M vs 1.3M (5.5x), u128 3.1M vs 604K (5.1x), u256 1.5M vs 263K (5.8x), Option<Struct> 7.7M vs 921K (8.3x), Vec<u32> (1000) 410K vs 91K (4.5x), Address 12.9M vs 1.9M (6.8x); the table's 'Average 5.2x' row does not match its own rows (arithmetic mean 6.5x, geometric mean 6.4x, derived from page data). Raw entrypoint: serializeInto 66 ns vs @mysten serialize 728 ns for SimpleStruct (11x), u64 36 vs 612 ns (17x), u256 100 vs 1,718 ns (17x), Vec<u32> (1000) 884 vs 9,275 ns (10x).
corrections.caveats: The speedup comes from pure TypeScript, not WebAssembly: src/codegen.ts generates straight-line serializers and deserializers with new Function(), and src/wasm.ts states 'All TypeScript hot paths use optimized pure-TS implementations; the WASM module is available for validation and specialized operations' (bcs-type.ts, bcs.ts, reader.ts, writer.ts and codegen.ts never call the bcs-zig WASM; a commit removed the 'dead wasm-schema'). new Function() codegen needs CSP 'unsafe-eval' in browsers. The raw table compares serializeInto, which skips validate() and writes into a caller buffer without allocation or bounds checks, against @mysten/bcs serialize, which validates and allocates, so it is not like-for-like. No benchmark harness in the repo; the linked live benchmark (bcs-benchmark.vercel.app) does not resolve; Bun version, @mysten/bcs version and hardware unstated. The README's 'Average 5.2x' row is inconsistent with its rows (mean 6.5x). All 15 commits were made on 2026-04-03; 1 star. Claims byte-identical output on @mysten/bcs's 244 tests (test/compat.test.ts).

notes: Numbers match the README, but the record's framing is wrong: the Zig/WASM module is bundled and exported (loadWasm) yet unused on every measured path, so this is a pure TypeScript runtime-codegen serializer beating another JS serializer. Recommend override name '@unconfirmed/bcs', language 'TypeScript (runtime codegen via new Function)', and either keep in wasm-libraries-and-apps with the shortcoming 'WASM not on measured path' or move to a JS serialization category; second shortcoming: no public harness, live benchmark host dead.

tier_reason: First-party README 'Speed' section with public harness benchmark.js (blake3 wasm, blake3 native, Node crypto md5/sha1/sha256 on zero-filled 64 B, 64 KB and 6 MB buffers) but only 'Node 12 on my MacBook': no CPU model, no Rust/wasm build flags.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 64 B: blake3 wasm 1,040,000 ops/sec vs Node sha256 271,000 (3.8x, derived from page data) and vs the library's native binding 625,000 (1.66x, derived from page data); 64 KB: blake3 wasm 6,410 vs sha256 6,470 (parity, wasm about 1% slower), native binding 48,900 (7.6x sha256, derived from page data); 6 MB: blake3 wasm 65.2 vs sha256 69.2 (wasm about 6% slower), native binding 502 (7.3x sha256, derived from page data). The page's parenthesised multipliers (15,900x etc.) are relative to the slowest row of the whole table (6 MB blake3 wasm), not to sha256.
corrections.caveats: The WebAssembly build beats Node's built-in sha256 and the same library's native binding only at 64 B, where per-call overhead dominates; at 64 KB it is at parity with sha256 and at 6 MB slower, while the native binding is 7-8x faster than both. The published numbers predate v3.0.0: they were taken on Node 12 with matcha when native bindings were 'a work in progress', whereas v3.0.0 (2022-10-08) requires Node 16, added SIMD to both the wasm and native builds and builds the native module with node-gyp, and the current benchmark.js uses benny, so the README table does not describe the shipped code. Hardware is an unnamed MacBook. Inputs are zero-filled Buffer.alloc buffers. Last commit 2022-10-09 (v3.0.0). This is a JavaScript binding (wasm plus native) of the official BLAKE3 Rust crate (blake3-src submodule).

notes: Numbers, MIT licence, 199 stars and last commit 2022-10-09 (abandoned, over 3 years) verified. Possible duplicate: a JS/wasm binding of BLAKE3 (https://github.com/blake3-team/blake3, wave 7 crypto-hashes, tier B); record decision duplicate unless wasm builds of listed libraries count as their own entries in wasm-libraries-and-apps. Shortcomings: wasm only faster at 64 B, numbers stale (pre-v3.0.0, Node 12, unnamed MacBook).

tier_reason: First-party README table; the harness bench/compare-blake3-fast.ts is public (blake3-jit vs @napi-rs/blake-hash 1.4.0, @huggingface/blake3-wasm and a blake3-fast build loaded from an untracked ../tmp path), but no CPU model, Node version or run command output are stated.

corrections.caveats: First-party; no hardware or Node version stated. Inputs below 4 KB (SIMD_THRESHOLD = 4 * CHUNK_LEN in src/hash.ts) run the pure JavaScript path, so every size where blake3-jit wins (96 B, 512 B, 1 KB) is pure JS beating napi call overhead, not WebAssembly; the runtime-generated WASM SIMD path (4 KB and above) is slower than the native addon (32 KB 1.36 vs 1.97 GB/s, 0.69x; 1 MB 1.38 vs 2.06 GB/s, 0.67x, derived from page data). The baseline @napi-rs/blake-hash is the same author's napi binding of the official blake3 Rust crate (a different implementation, not the same code compiled natively). The harness also times @huggingface/blake3-wasm (a wasm-vs-wasm comparison) and blake3-fast, but the README publishes only the napi column; the blake3-fast build is loaded from ../tmp and is not in the repo. Correctness of the timed paths is checked only on a 5-byte input in the harness.

notes: Numbers, MIT licence, 35 stars, 122 commits and last commit 2026-10-07 (renovate bot; active) verified. Shortcoming for this category: the WASM part never beats native; wins are pure-JS small-input FFI-overhead wins. baseline_in_list left false; the napi baseline wraps the listed BLAKE3 crate (wave 7) if the orchestrator wants to treat it as an in-list baseline.
